description:
Basic Information

  • Full Project Title: Mathematical Biology and Population Dynamics
  • Host Institution: University of Birmingham
  • Department: School of Mathematics
  • Study Level: PhD
  • Duration: 3 to 3.5 years, full time
  • Start Date: 2026/27 academic year
  • Funding Type: College or EPSRC scholarship (competitive)
  • Annual Stipend: £21,805 tax-free (2026/27 UKRI rate)
  • Tuition Fees: Covered for scholarship recipients
  • Eligibility: UK, EU and international applicants
  • Application Deadline: 24 October 2026 (23:59 UK time)
  • Note: Chinese candidates can also apply through the CSC–University of Birmingham joint PhD scholarships

Project Description

This project involves developing mathematical models to study population dynamics in biological systems. The research will combine dynamical systems theory, mathematical modelling, and data-driven methods to explore how populations change over time in response to ecological interactions, environmental changes, and other biological processes. The studentship is hosted by the School of Mathematics, where mathematical biology sits within the Applied Mathematics PhD programme.

Funding and Benefits

  • Annual stipend: £21,805 per year, tax-free, at the UKRI minimum doctoral rate for 2026/27 (effective 1 October 2026), paid for the 3–3.5 year duration of the award.
  • Tuition fees: fully covered for scholarship recipients.
  • Self-funded route: strong self-funded international applicants will be considered, and exceptionally strong candidates may be awarded a tuition fee waiver for up to three years, as stated in the official advert.
  • Research environment: successful candidates join the School of Mathematics and the University of Birmingham Doctoral School, which provides tailored researcher development, wellbeing support, global opportunities and career preparation.

Who Can Apply

  • Academic entry: a 2:1 honours degree (or equivalent) in a Mathematics-related subject, or a lower degree plus an MSc or substantial relevant experience — the standard entry requirement for Birmingham Mathematics PhD programmes.
  • English language: IELTS Academic 6.0 overall with no less than 5.5 in any band (the University of Birmingham standard requirement; TOEFL iBT, PTE Academic and other accepted tests are also recognised).
  • Funding eligibility: the College or EPSRC scholarship is available to UK and EU candidates. International candidates are considered as strong self-funded applicants, and exceptionally strong candidates may receive a tuition fee waiver for up to three years.
  • Chinese candidates: the CSC–University of Birmingham PhD Scholarships programme offers 10 joint-funded scholarships each year, alongside the CSC national scholarship portal (csc.edu.cn).

How to Apply

  1. Identify the right programme: this studentship sits within the Applied Mathematics PhD at the School of Mathematics.
  2. Make informal contact with the school before applying — informal enquiries are strongly encouraged. Email: maths.pgr@contacts.bham.ac.uk
  3. Submit the University of Birmingham online PhD application. You will normally provide academic transcripts, degree certificates, a CV, academic references and a short research statement.
  4. Apply before the deadline: 24 October 2026 (23:59 UK time). Early applications are strongly recommended as the award is competitive.

Chinese candidates: also review the CSC – University of Birmingham PhD Scholarships page for the 10 joint-funded awards.
